notes:
I wasn't able to research Psalm 127, so I don't have any notes for you.

My first attempt tried to load seven commentary pages at once, and it went over the tool's usage limit. When I retried with just one page, I was told I had no more tool calls left for this turn. Nothing loaded, not even the Enduring Word page, so I haven't read any of the sources.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and never fill gaps from my own knowledge. Since I've read nothing, writing verse-by-verse notes now would mean making them up and attaching URLs I never opened. So I've left it blank rather than guess.

**When you send the request again** (the limit should reset with a new message), I'll load the pages one at a time instead of all together. I plan to read them in this order:

1. **Traditional reading:** Enduring Word (Psalm 127); Bible Hub's Gill, Ellicott and Pulpit Commentary pages on Psalm 127; Precept Austin's Psalm 127 commentary; Spurgeon's *Treasury of David* (via spurgeon.org or Bible Hub/StudyLight).
2. **Where Protestant traditions differ:** For verses 3–5, I'll look for articles on children, family size and birth control, and on the "Quiverfull" movement, from Desiring God, The Gospel Coalition, Ligonier, GotQuestions and LCMS. I'll also check Wesley's notes on wesley.nnu.edu.
3. **Other views:** NET Bible translator notes (for example on "sleep" in verse 2 and "the gate" in verse 5); Augustine's exposition on New Advent (he numbers it Psalm 126); catholic.com on openness to children; and anything the allowed sites say about prosperity-style readings of verse 2.

Just reply "go ahead" and I'll start.
